reason: Tried to break it and could not. Downloaded Project Gutenberg #6408 (Garnett, 1920) and read it in place: lines 1533 to 1534 print “What is needed is constant work, day and night, constant reading, study, will.... Every hour is precious for it.... Come to us, smash the vodka bottle”, under the heading TO HIS BROTHER NIKOLAY. / MOSCOW, / 1886. (line 1440), directly after the eight conditions of cultured people. Every word matches Garnett; no drift toward the later Yarmolinsky or Karlinsky renderings. The one thing to know: the four dots after “will” are Chekhov's own suspension points as Garnett prints them (the Russian has “воля… Тут дорог каждый час…”), not an omission; the shipped “will. … Every hour” is a fair typographic rendering (full stop plus ellipsis) and nothing is left out, but a reader will take the ellipsis for a cut. A note saying the ellipsis is Chekhov's own, or printing it closed up as “will.… Every hour”, would be more honest; this is style, not a wording fault. The closing “for it....” is truncated to a full stop, which the ending rule requires. Attribution is Chekhov in his own voice. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Chekhov at 1 of 3 (month 1 only), not banned. In scope: a private letter of 1886, translation published 1920.
